assessments.reasoning: The full text/MIT.txt came from the SPDX license-list-data repository at commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. Its 1,078-byte length and SHA-256 b05785f9f18e6716bab63424b11454513b9943a222595b70411009202fc592b5 agree with the measured archive input. Its literal notice occupies the claimed interval. The changed-input refusal challenges the assumption that a different file would serve as the same input.

The full 8,433-byte json/details/MIT.json came from the same pinned SPDX commit. Its SHA-256 0c2b3c87a154a4aaac6bc6a735dd454dc29d9a78c23a85deedb080e0c65de1f8 matches the reproduction. The relevant field is licenseText. Decoding its escapes yields the literal notice placeholders, line breaks and final LF. The reproduction tested whether that field differed from the archive plaintext and found byte-for-byte equality. The separate template and HTML fields have different contents and provide no basis for that equality.

challenge.method: Examined the reproduction's changed-input digest check, incomplete holder/year check and existing-destination check alongside its successful fresh write. Also compared the decoded JSON licenseText with the measured archive input and examined the renderer checks for absent and duplicated placeholders.
challenge.results: The CLI refused the changed input and the incomplete notice pair, and preserved the existing destination. The renderer also refused inputs containing zero or duplicate placeholders. Those outcomes establish boundaries on the successful write. No challenge contradicted the claim under its stated conditions.

limitations: The observation covers one input revision, CLI commit, runtime, holder, year and fresh destination.
The fixture establishes no author permission, rights to redistribute license data, or conclusions about retaining notices in an existing work.

reasoning: The complete 2,002-byte claim identifies revision 1 and its reported SHA-256 matches the frozen claim digest. The reproduction ran public CLI commit 4c67e9b85e218fe40e9b17f2bde7fb90da0b552b on win32 with Python 3.13.5. Its method SHA-256 matches the claim. With holder Example Project, year 2026 and a new scratch destination, the CLI wrote a file and the exact-write check verified its contents. The file measured 1,072 bytes with SHA-256 0196f81d7f82a887642e004cb0703c3069eb35bc493fdce129dd449f8ed092af. In the original plaintext, 13 bytes precede the notice and byte 53 is its terminating LF. Replacing the 40 bytes in [13,53) with the 34-byte notice for the fixture accounts for the six-byte reduction. The exact-output and exact-write checks support preservation of the line ending and all surrounding bytes. The two preview checks were separate observations.

reproduction.reason: The tool ran the real pinned CLI, verified a written scratch file, and matched the byte-level control.
